claim: Let \(G\) be an infinite countable group equipped with a proper right-invariant metric, and let \((X_i,T_i,G)\) be nonempty compact metrizable \(G\)-systems. Put \(X=\prod_{i\ge1}X_i\) with the coordinatewise action and let \(d\) be any compatible metric for the product topology. If infinitely many \(X_i\) are non-singletons, then for every \(\varepsilon>0\) there exist distinct \(x,y\in X\) such that \(d(T^g x,T^g y)<\varepsilon\) for every \(g\in G\). Consequently every horofunction is \(\varepsilon\)-non-deterministic for every \(\varepsilon>0\): \(\operatorname{ND}_{\varepsilon}(X)=\operatorname{ND}(X)=\partial(G,\rho)\). In particular, the product action is not expansive. More generally, the countable product action is expansive exactly when only finitely many factors are non-singletons and each of those non-singleton factor actions is expansive.
integrity: The proof is self-contained apart from using the cited definition of horofunction non-determinism. Literature non-hits are treated only as supporting originality evidence. The conflict with the 2014 countable-product expansiveness theorem is stated explicitly rather than ignored.
scientific_limitations: The maximal non-determinism theorem is for coordinatewise countable products of nonempty compact metrizable systems.
It does not cover skew products with coordinate coupling or nonmetrizable uncountable products.

The countable-tail mechanism is elementary, so an older equivalent global-nonexpansiveness lemma may exist under different terminology even though no checked source states the horofunction conclusion.
title: Countable products force maximal horoball non-determinism
